headline: Vendor booths
lead: Food trucks, open cooking, drinks, snacks, craft and merchant booths, and nonprofit info tables for Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết 2027.

meta.description: Apply for a vendor booth on Eventeny and learn the two-round application process for Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết 2027 — apply, selection, offer, pay, or waitlist / decline.

waitlist.title: Apply on Eventeny
waitlist.body: Booth applications are open on Eventeny. There are four applications: **Food booths & trucks**, **Merchants & corporate exhibitors**, **Nonprofit, community info**, and **Free kids activity tables** — pick the one that fits your booth. **Round 1 closes Nov 5.**

cta.label: Apply on Eventeny
cta.note: You’ll sign in or create a free Eventeny account, then pay the $25 application deposit when you apply. Nonprofit, community info, and kids activity tables pay no deposit, and the free kids activity application doesn’t ask for a card or bank account.

inventory.title: Booth inventory
inventory.intro: Seat counts are **tentative** planning caps for ~6,000 weekend attendance. Final caps are set at Round 1 decisions (Nov 10), after park capacity confirmation with Cosumnes CSD. Weekend fees match Eventeny.

rows: Field drinks (2 boba/matcha · 1 sugarcane · 1 aguas · 1 coffee)
Shared pad pool — corporate / marketing · merchant, craft, and snack / treat · nonprofit / mission and kids-owned

notes: **Open food seats are split by menu style** so no one style floods the field: about **4** fast handheld (bánh mì, tacos, skewers), **5** rice plates and bowls, **4** noodle, wok, or soup, and **2** BBQ or smoked — down from about 20 hot-food vendors in 2026.
Drinks are **exclusivity-capped** by category (counts in the table above).

**Limited spots per food type.** Beyond menu-style and drink caps, we will likely limit how many booths sell the same food or snack type so guests get variety and every vendor has a fair shot. We can’t publish which types will be capped yet — those limits firm up as applications come in. When more than one vendor applies for a limited type, we rank applications and offer the booth in that order; if the first pick doesn’t pay, the next ranked vendor gets the offer.
The **60**-pad shared pool is one inventory — corporate, goods/snack, nonprofit info, and free kids activity tables compete for the same seats (not separate caps).
inventory.footnote: Seat counts are set at Round 1 decisions (Nov 10), after park capacity confirmation.

fees.title: Fees and terms
fees.intro: Fees are weekend totals (**$/day × 2 days**), the same rates listed on Eventeny. No early-bird discount — early apply buys **certainty** in Round 1.

sections.title: Application deposit
body: Food, merchant, craft, and corporate booths pay **$25** when you apply.
bullets: Accepted → credited toward your booth fee
Not selected → refunded
Selected but unpaid by the pay-by → forfeited; booth goes to the next waitlisted vendor
Round 1 no-pay → Round 2 waitlist, no new deposit

sections.title: Nonprofit and kids tables
bullets: Nonprofit / community info: **no** application deposit; $75 only if approved
Free kids activity (guests not charged): **Free kids activity tables** app — no fee, no card
Paid kids activity → **Merchant / craft** ($150)

sections.title: Locking your booth
body: A selection holds only through the pay-by. **Booth fee locks the seat** — not cleanup deposits.
bullets: **Round 1 — on-site cooking (food truck / open cook):** pay **$500 of the $750** booth fee by **Fri, Nov 20, 2026** to lock. Remaining booth fee (**$225** after your $25 application credit) plus cleanup deposits due **Fri, Jan 29, 2027**, or you yield the booth
**Round 1 — everyone else:** pay the **full booth fee** by **Fri, Nov 20, 2026** to lock. Cleanup deposits due **Fri, Jan 29, 2027**
**Round 2:** pay booth fee (and any deposits due) by **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** (or at approval if later)

sections.title: Trash and cooking deposits
body: Food, merchant, and corporate booths also pay refundable cleanup deposits. Charged **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** (or at approval if later) — not used to lock the booth.
bullets: **$100 trash** — every food, merchant, and corporate booth
**$500 cooking cleanup** — on-site cooking only (trucks/trailers, open flame, grills, fryers)
Pre-packaged / no-cook → trash only
after: Refunded when you bag out and leave the space clean; cooking cleanup refunded if there’s no grease, oil, or burn marks.

sections.title: Temporary Food Facility (TFF) permit
body: Food, drink, snack, and sealed take-home food booths need a Sacramento County EMD Temporary Food Facility permit for the festival weekend. This is **not** part of the booth fee — we pass the County fee through at cost.
bullets: Already hold a valid multi-event (MEV) or mobile food facility (MFF) permit that covers this event → provide your permit number; no TFF fee
Need a single-event TFF → we file with the County and charge the County fee as a pass-through: **$116** pre-packaged / low risk · **$258** food prep / high risk (FY 2026–27 EMD rates)
Charged after approval when we assemble the event package (typically with the Jan 29 deposits)

sections.title: Cancellations and refunds
body: Cancel by **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** → we refund booth fees you’ve paid, minus a **cancel fee of 25% of the booth fee (minimum $50)**. After that date, **no booth-fee refund** — the festival is set around your booth.
Elk Grove Park is our planned venue; permits are in progress. If the festival can’t proceed there, we refund deposits and booth fees in full (no cancel fee).
Weather: each canceled festival day earns a **2028 credit** for half the booth fee — not cash. Weather earns a credit; only a venue cancellation is refunded in cash.

sections.title: Insurance
bullets: **Food or power/generator:** upload a general liability COI with the application — we check it before confirmation
**Basic non-food, no power:** sign the vendor agreement confirming you carry your own liability insurance
after: Additional-insured wording is finalized in your acceptance email.

sections.title: Hours and load-in
bullets: Vendor hours: **11 AM–7 PM** Sat–Sun, Feb 13–14, 2027
Load-in: **Friday, Feb 12, 2027**
Tear-down: after 7 PM Sunday
after: Exact load-in and tear-down times come with your acceptance email.

timeline.title: How selection works
timeline.intro: We run a **two-round** process so early applicants can lock a seat with certainty, while we still hold room for strong late applications. The path is the same in both rounds.

rounds.label: Round 1 — Priority
rounds.note: Most seats (~70–80%). Decisions around Nov 10. **Booth fee locks the seat** by Nov 20: on-site cooks pay **$500 of $750**; everyone else pays the full booth fee. Miss Nov 20 → forfeit the $25 deposit and move to the Round 2 selection waitlist (no new deposit). Cooks’ remaining booth fee + cleanup deposits due Jan 29, or yield.

rounds.label: Round 2 — Open
rounds.note: Remaining seats (~20–30%) plus any Round 1 seats that don’t pay on time. Decisions around Jan 22 — including waitlisted Round 1 selectees. Pay by Jan 29. **Food and snack applicants:** wait until we publish the Round 1 food vendors and their menus before you apply — that list shows what’s already taken, so you can tell whether your type would land on a waitlist or whether you should apply to sell something different.

timeline.pathIntro: Every applicant waits for a decision batch. From there:

steps.title: Apply
steps.body: Submit through Eventeny with the $25 application deposit (required to be considered; nonprofit, community info, and kids activity tables pay no deposit). Food and power booths upload a certificate of insurance with the application.

steps.title: Wait for selection
steps.body: We review the round’s pool together — not first-come, first-served. Food booths are ranked for menu fit; other booths by staff fit.

steps.title: One of three outcomes
steps.body: You’ll land on one of these paths.

outcomes.title: Offer sent
outcomes.body: You’re selected. Accept the offer (food vendors may get a recommended festival menu), then **pay the booth-fee lock by the pay-by date** (Round 1 cooks: $500 of $750 by Nov 20; everyone else: full booth fee by Nov 20).
outcomes.next: Once the lock payment clears, you’re on the map. Round 1 cooks still owe remaining booth fee + cleanup deposits by Jan 29.

outcomes.title: Selection waitlist
outcomes.body: You’re a ranked runner-up for that lane — **or** you were selected in Round 1 but didn’t make the Nov 20 lock payment. Unpaid Round 1 selectees are moved here automatically and **must wait for Round 2 decisions** (around Jan 22). **If you weren’t first pick for a limited food type,** you can stay on this waitlist (in case the first vendor doesn’t pay or drops out), **or** submit a new Round 2 application for a different food type that isn’t already represented.
outcomes.next: A waitlist spot is not a reserved booth until you receive an offer and pay.

outcomes.title: Declined
outcomes.body: Not selected for this festival season. If you paid the $25 application deposit, it is refunded.

steps.title: Pay → official vendor
steps.body: Selection holds only through the pay-by date. Pay on time and you’re on the map. **Miss Round 1’s Nov 20 booth-fee lock** and you forfeit the $25 deposit and are placed (no new deposit needed) on the **Round 2 selection waitlist**. **Round 1 cooks** who locked with $500 but miss the **Jan 29** remainder + deposits **yield the booth**. Cancel by Jan 29 for a booth-fee refund minus the cancel fee; after that, no booth-fee refund.

timeline.footnote: Dates are planning targets published for vendors. Seat counts by booth type are set at Round 1 decisions (Nov 10).

criteria.title: Selection criteria
criteria.intro: We pick from each round’s full pool — not first paid. Food applicants are ranked inside their lane; craft, merchant, and info booths use staff fit review.
criteria.factorsIntro: Working weights for open-cook and drink applicants — we may fine-tune them before Round 1 decisions (Nov 10).

rows: Compelling menu offering / festival fit — see [Food menu](/food-menu/) for examples
Booth economics (can this lane succeed at our attendance)
Focused brand (clear specialty vs sprawling menu)
Dietary and guest-need coverage — see [Food menu](/food-menu/) for examples
Social media presence (active food posts — not just a handle or follower count)

criteria.factorsNote: Deposit timing only breaks ties when scores are equal. Other soft factors (local Elk Grove connection, cultural anchors) may also apply at smaller weights.
deny: Adult-oriented businesses or products — including tobacco, drugs, pornography, firearms, and dating services
Organizations that practice or promote discrimination in employment or services
criteria.salesIntro: Even approved vendors may not display or sell:
sales: Firecrackers, fireworks, firearms, weapons, or other dangerous items
Vulgar, offensive, sexually explicit, or obscene materials
criteria.footnote: We may ask you to remove any product or service we deem unsuitable for a family festival. That call is final.
